newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises on Diablo Canyon outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises on Diablo Canyon outage.

text.p: NYMEX electricity prices rose Wednesday on news of an outage at a California nuclear power plant, industry sources said.

The 1,073 Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit in Avila Beach on California's central coast was taken off line at about 0500 PDT/0800 EDT Wednesday, and was being kept on hot standby, which means the reactor is still active and typically indicates plant engineers expect the outage to be brief.
A spokesman said the unit was taken off line to correct a problem in the feedwater system, and said it was not yet known how long it would be shut.
The facility's neighboring unit, Diablo Canyon 1, rated at 1,087 MW, was still operating at full power, he said.
News of the outage pushed power futures values higher.

As of 1230 EDT, August Palo Verde futures were trading up 76 cents at $34.30 following exchanges in a range of $34.00-35.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), while September was 35 cents higher at $28.75 following trades in a range of $28.40-29.10 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 37 cents at $23.30 following exchanges in a range of $23.00-23.40, while September was up 40 cents at the day's high of $23.30 after trade as low as 23.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1130 EDT an estimated total of 88 COB and 184 PV contracts had traded.
Also in generation news, Southern California Edison Co's 1,070 MW San Onofre unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
San Onofre 2 was shut Sunday to replace its charge line check valves, and San Onofre 3 has been out of service since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
As of 1210 EDT August Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down three cents at $2.076 per million British thermal units.

Meteorologists called for a warming trend to begin later this week in the Pacific Northwest following recent cooler-than-normal weather. Meanwhile, forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to stay near to above normal through next week.
NYMEX markets will close early Thursday in advance of the July 4 Independence Day holiday, with PV closing at 1255 EDT and COB ending trade at 1300 EDT.
COB open interest for July 1 rose 92 to 6,235 while PV open interest rose 96 to 6,097, NYMEX said.
